extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, sketch writers, and comedy performers/writers learning craft and room culture
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, writer-facing guidance and an informal rubric for creating jokes, sketches, and stage choices drawing on Tina Fey's Bossypants and SNL writers-room practices. Focuses on improv rules, specificity, voice, draft-and-edit workflow, and live performance presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does each beat agree-and-add to the previous?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does each beat agree-and-add to the previous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fey-style beat-to-beat construction: each moment should accept the previous offer and build on it (agree-and-add). This keeps momentum and coherence; useful both in improv and in sketch joke structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make declarative statements (not questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comedian making declarative statements? / Make statements — don't ask questions; make declarative additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer assertive lines that advance the premise or character rather than asking the audience or other characters for direction. Declarative choices clarify point of view and create stronger setups and payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert mistakes into choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Are mistakes converted into choices? / There are no mistakes, only opportunities — turn errors into choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When something goes wrong in performance or a draft, reinterpret it as a new offer rather than a failure. Use unexpected moments as material instead of apologizing or abandoning them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke specific (not generic)? / Specificity always.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, particular details rather than generic labels or abstractions; specific images and actions make jokes sharper and funnier. (Example guidance from Fey: to make an audience laugh vs. to make comedy writers laugh—specific staging choices differ.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view / voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it have point of view? / Voice (point of view) > generic jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinct comedic voice or POV is more valuable than interchangeable one-liners. Establish who is speaking and why their perspective matters to the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch up; self-deprecating that does not punch down
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecating humor that punches up, not down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim humor at targets with more power or keep the tone self-aware without attacking vulnerable groups. Self-deprecation should feel like punching up (or equalizing) rather than harming those with less power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace first draft then ruthlessly cut
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace the imperfect "first draft" then ruthlessly cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow messy initial writing to generate material, but be prepared to edit aggressively afterward. Generate lots of options, then tighten and remove anything that doesn't serve the joke or beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't tell the audience to laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't tell the audience to laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cues such as 'Isn't that funny?' or instructing the audience; instead, trust the material and performance choices to produce the laugh organically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to the choice; intensity matches risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to the choice — even if uncertain. The crazier the choice, the harder the commitment must be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a character or joke choice is made, play it fully. Riskier, more unusual choices require even stronger commitment to sell them and make them land.

rubrics_metrics.name: High joke quota and rapid iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: High joke quota and rapid iteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In environments like SNL, writers are expected to produce many ideas quickly and iterate rapidly. Quantity + quick edits increase the chance of strong material and fits room expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for rough rewrite tables / vigorous peer critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly competitive, "rough" rewrite tables; sketches torn apart sketch-by-sketch by colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect drafts to be deconstructed in group editing. Design work to survive dissection, and learn to use critique to strengthen the piece rather than taking it personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching is impersonal / anonymous-feeling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches may feel anonymous or impersonal in a writers' room. Treat pitch rejections as process noise: refine ideas and keep submitting rather than relying on any single pitch.
